version.changelog: v2.3 quality enhancement - security audit + marketing packaging + slug-content validation

llm.summary: This is a code-assistant skill with expected read and command capabilities, but it describes broad command, file-writing, and external API behavior without enough clear scoping or user control.

dimensions.detail: The skill declares read and exec tools and advertises command execution, network troubleshooting, file parsing/writing, and API integration; those capabilities are high-impact and under-scoped for a broadly-triggered basic assistant.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact is a single SKILL.md with no bundled executable scripts, dependency installer, or install-time behavior found in the inspected workspace.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Activation language covers broad programming, debugging, testing, deployment, and automation workflows, while the runtime instructions do not clearly require per-action consent or define command/file/API boundaries.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence mechanism, background worker, scheduled task, memory poisoning, or privilege escalation instructions were found, but command execution could still affect the local environment depending on agent enforcement.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is programming delegation, so reading code and running commands can fit, but the document expands into file writes, deployment/debugging, network checks, and external API integration beyond a narrow basic code-generation helper.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill before installing. It is not malicious from the inspected artifacts, but it should only be used where a programming assistant is allowed to read project files and run commands, and users should require explicit approval before command execution, file changes, or any external API/network activity.
llm.findings:
[SDI-1] unexpected: The mismatch concern is supported: the artifact begins as a basic code-delegation skill but later advertises generic file writes, API integration, and command execution.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The broad trigger concern is supported because the description includes ordinary code generation, programming help, debugging/testing, and deployment despite exec access.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese interaction support is disclosed and appears to be a locale/support statement, not a security issue by itself.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The credential/network concern is supported in part: the skill says no extra API key is needed except external APIs, while also describing HTTPS/network/API behavior without concrete endpoints or data-flow limits.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The file-modification concern is supported because an example says generated docstrings are merged into complete code and the later feature list says file writing is supported, without review or rollback requirements.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The external API claim is under-specified relative to the declared read/exec tool surface and lacks endpoint, data handling, and consent details.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The warning concern is supported because command execution and API/network use are advertised, but user-facing system impact and outbound data exposure warnings are only generic.
